$comment: Bayan <-> OpenTelemetry GenAI crosswalk. This file exists so that OTel semantic-convention churn costs a mapping update rather than a schema break (PRD R-F8). The core Bayan schema contains NO OTel identifiers.

otelSemconv.warning: As of Sep 2026 no gen_ai.* span, metric or attribute is marked Stable. The conventions were reportedly deprecated in semconv v1.42.0 and removed in v1.43.0, relocating to open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai. The MOVE is confirmed from the official semconv redirect notice; the version numbers are from a third-party source and are UNVERIFIED. Re-pin before shipping.

direction: bayan -> otel (emit); reverse mapping is lossy and not defined

mappings.note: Bayan enum is a superset; unmapped values emit as-is
Bayan carries a DIGEST, OTel carries a NAME. Not interchangeable; emit both or neither
OTel is an array; Bayan is scalar
No OTel equivalent. Bucketing is a Bayan minimisation control (R-F7)
Bayan value is HMAC'd; OTel's is typically raw. NEVER emit the raw value to satisfy OTel
Tier 3 in Bayan. Suppressed by default despite OTel treating it as ordinary metadata
Not an attribute. OTel's off-span content upload path is the architectural equivalent: the span holds a reference, the content lives in a separate store. This is the seam Bayan puts a reviewer on
OTel retrieval spans carry no document-identity convention. Bayan's pseudonymisation requirement has no OTel counterpart
No OTel equivalent, and this is correct: OTel has no notion of a field too sensitive to export
No OTel equivalent. This is the central gap that makes Bayan a separate schema rather than an OTel profile

explicitlyNotMapped.gen_ai.input.messages: Tier 4 content. Never enters a fingerprint.
explicitlyNotMapped.gen_ai.output.messages: Tier 4 content. Never enters a fingerprint.
explicitlyNotMapped.gen_ai.system_instructions: Vendor artefact but potentially client-tuned; carry as promptVersion digest instead.
